label: Fugue in C major, BWV 531
caution: Read from Tobi's MusicXML file (Tobis Notenarchiv), notes, ties and names as they stand there; the voices were sorted by this program from the file's staves, stems and beams, and have not been proofread note by note. The pedal's line is the bass. The writing is loose: the left hand's single line makes both the third and the fourth entries, and the pedal plays only now and then.
title: Prelude and Fugue in C major, BWV 531: Fugue
procedures: a voice held back until after the exposition

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject. Alto: free counterpoint. Tenor: a figure from the subject (2 times).
sections.leads: From C major to F major

sections.label: Episode 2
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject (3 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence rising by a sixth every bar. Alto: the opening of the subject (2 times) and a figure from the subject and a figure from the subject, inverted. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and a figure from the subject (2 times). Bass: free counterpoint. Returns in Episode 6 (bars 43–44).
sections.leads: From F major to G major

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted and a figure from the subject, in a sequence falling by a step every half bar. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted. Tenor: a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a fifth every half bar. Bass: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a step every half bar.
sections.leads: From G major to C major

Tenor: a figure from the subject (5 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every half bar. Bass: free counterpoint.

Episode 5

sections.leads: Between two statements in C major; perfect cadence in E minor at bar 41

sections.label: Episode 6
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 2 (bars 11–16) in part, with the soprano's line in the alto, the alto's line in the tenor, at the same pitch level. sections.leads: From C major to G major
